text:
wrote /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-guillaumeloulier-PhpstormProjects-oss-elephc--claude-worktrees-streams-csv-signature/c8dbe38f-1f79-484f-9b83-62bacab9ca56/scratchpad/obj/glob_wrapper_type.py: """A `glob://` directory reported `plainfile` where php reports `glob`.

MEASURED on `php -n` 8.5.6:

    stream_get_meta_data(opendir("glob://" . $dir . "/*"))
    php:    wrapper_type='glob'   stream_type='glob'
    elephc: wrapper_type='plainfile' stream_type='glob'

`stream_type` was already right, because its namer asks the BACKEND KIND first and a glob directory
has its own. `wrapper_type` asked only the recorded wrapper id, which `opendir()` never stamps — so
it stayed at the unset value 0, and the table maps 0 to `plainfile`.

Asking the backend kind here too fixes the computed path as
